To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the parameters used in a reality-based vibration model can be modified based upon human perception to enhance the realism of haptic displays for impact events; and (2) the modified parameters can be used to differentiate between materials in virtual environments.

the bandwidth of the stylus in the haptic display limits the ability to display reality-based vibrations, and perceptual experiments with the haptic device can be used to modify reality-based vibration parameters to enhance the realism of vibration feedback.

the acceleration of a haptic device is not a good predictor of the perceived vibration feedback of impact events and that a modified decaying sinusoidal wave model is a more effective vibration feedback model than one derived strictly from acceleration measurements.

the development of a vibration model for impact events and its application to the haptic display.
the development of a vibration model that can be used for haptic feedback to improve the realism of virtual environments.
enhancing the realism of vibration feedback in virtual environments by creating a vibration model based on acceleration measurements and modifying the model through perceptual experiments.
